highlights.title: Add FreeStyle Libre 3/3+ support
changes: FreeStyle Libre 3/3+ can be selected and paired directly from Trio's CGM settings.
Home glucose view now shows sensor lifecycle details, including warmup countdown and expiry progress.
Alerts generated by the LibreLoop plugin are shown in Trio and routed through the app's alert system.
Libre 3/3+ support is marked experimental and does not provide 1‑minute readings (normal 5‑minute cadence expected).

highlights.title: Updated loop indicator spinner
changes: The loop indicator now shows an animated capsule-style spinner instead of a static label or default progress view.
The looping label is shown only while the spinner is actively animating and is rendered verbatim (not localized).
The spinner animation is smoother and enforces a short minimum spin time to avoid flicker when starting or stopping.
A reusable CapsuleSpinner component replaces the previous spinner and the capsule outline thickness was adjusted for a清.

highlights.title: Show release notes in the app
changes: Home now shows a “New Release” panel when your installed version has unread release notes.
Tapping the panel opens a full-sheet that summarizes what changed and any important safety callouts.
Release Notes are also available from Settings, including a list of previous versions to browse.
Notes are fetched from GitHub with a bundled offline fallback so the notes can load without internet.
Tapping the sheet’s acknowledge button hides the Home panel for that specific version; viewing from Settings does not.

highlights.title: Show quick-pick bolus with one decimal
changes: Quick-pick bolus suggestions now display with a single decimal place.
Suggested amounts are floored to one decimal (rounded down) instead of rounded to nearest.
This prevents the suggestion pill from showing two fractional digits.

includedPullRequests.title: Add Libre 3/3+
includedPullRequests.body:
## Summary
  - Integrates the LibreLoop CGM plugin (with adaptations to work with pre `next-dev` LoopKit) so Trio can pair FreeStyle Libre 3 / 3+ sensors directly (no internet reliance, no external app).
  - Ships as three new submodules (`LibreLoop`, `LibreCRKit`, `LoopAlgorithm`) wired through Trio's existing `PluginManager` / `PluginSource` path.
  - Adds Libre 3 / 3+ to the CGM picker and surfaces sensor lifecycle + status highlight on the home glucose view via the shared CGM highlight pipeline.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> 1-min readings are currently not supported
> **This is still experimental**

  ## Test plan
  - [x] Fresh install → CGM settings → Libre 3 / 3+ visible in picker
  - [x] Pair a new Libre 3 / 3+ sensor and complete warmup
  - [x] Glucose values arrive on a normal 5-min cadence; no gaps > 6 min under steady conditions
  - [x] Backfill on cold-start / relaunch fills the last 24 h of history
  - [x] Sensor progress bobble on home view matches remaining lifetime; flips to grace period near expiry
  - [x] Alerts from LibreLoop (sensor issue, expiring, expired) show up
  - [x] Swap between Libre 3 / 3+ and another CGM (e.g. G7) and back — no stuck state (watch out, not down Receiver ID before removing Libre) 
  - [x] Loop enacts against Libre readings; no regressions vs. current Trio behaviour
  - [x] Simulator scenarios still work

includedPullRequests.title: Show Release Notes for Installed Trio Version
includedPullRequests.body: ## Summary Surfaces Trio's release notes in two places: - **Home** — a "New Release" entry in the multi-use panel, opening a sheet the user acknowledges to dismiss it - **Settings → Release Notes** — the current release, plus a **Previous Versions** screen for earlier ones ## Where the notes come from Three sources, in order of preference: 1. A live fetch of the GitHub releases API, since notes are sometimes edited after publishing 2. The last successful fetch, cached 3. A copy bundled at build time by `scripts/capture-release-notes.sh` The bundle covers **every stable release back to the last major or minor bump**, building `0.8.4` embeds `0.8.0` through `0.8.4`, so the list still works on a phone that has never been online. That script can never fail a build. A missing release, an unreachable GitHub, an unparseable version or an empty environment all simply leave the fallback out; every path exits 0, and a stale bundle from a previous version is removed rather than left behind. Drafts, prereleases, anything newer than the running build, and anything before `0.8.0` are all excluded. Sorting is by version. ## What the sheet renders The release's opening prose, its GitHub alert callouts, and the bullets under **"What's Changed At A Glance"**. The full notes, including the pull request lists, stay on GitHub behind a link. Two things worth knowing, both found by testing the parser against real releases rather than assuming a format: - **The "At A Glance" heading is not universal.** Five of the six most recent releases have it; the `0.8.3` hotfix used "What happened" / "What's fixed" instead. Relying on that heading alone would have produced an empty sheet on exactly the kind of urgent hotfix people most need to read, so the parser falls back to the release's opening prose. - **Releases carry `[!IMPORTANT]` callouts with safety-relevant content** — *"If you are using Medtrum Nano please update at your earliest convenience"*, *"your active Pod will be automatically transitioned"*. A bullets-only sheet would have hidden these behind a browser link, so they are parsed and shown. ## Acknowledgement Stored per version, so installing a newer release surfaces the panel again with nothing needing to reset it. Only the sheet's button acknowledges — swiping it away, or browsing notes from Settings, leaves the panel in place. The panel ranks below every warning state and above the stats. `MultiUsePanelState.resolve` gained a parameter, so its existing tests were updated and three added for the new ordering; all 10 pass. ### Screenshots | ☾ Release Panel | ☀ Release Panel | Settings Row | Release Notes | |--------|--------|--------|--------| | | | | |

includedPullRequests.title: Fix mmol/L rounding when importing a Nightscout profile during onboarding
includedPullRequests.body:
Importing a Nightscout profile in mmol/L during onboarding shifts some values up by 0.1, for example an ISF of 5.6 is imported and shown as 5.7. Fixes #1179.

The cause is correctUnitParsingOffsets, which rounds odd mg/dL values up to the next even number after the mmol/L conversion. It dates from the old settings import, where the mmol picker only contained even mg/dL values and imported values were matched exactly, so odd values had to be moved onto the even grid. The current picker contains one value per 0.1 mmol step and the import picks the closest value, so the converted value already lands on the right step and the bump just moves it into the next one.

includedPullRequests.title: Update TreatmentsRootView.swift to fix wrong field order
includedPullRequests.body:
It looks like some point in the past, the fat and protein field got exchanged. However, their order appears to be wrong. As a result, when using the UP ^ and DOWN arrow buttons that now appear with Liquid Glass (next to the trashcan) when you have the keyboard open: they return to the wrong fields. When you tap "up" on fat, it goes to protein to the right, and "up" on protein returns to Carbs instead of to the Fat field to the left. 

In other words the order defined in previousField and nextField appears to be incorrect. This commit re-orders them so the up and down arrows (and any other scenario wherein the order matters) should be fixed. (Works for me on iOS 26 and fixes the observed wrong order. Not tested on iOS 27.)

changes: Shows a startup warning when the app was built from any branch other than main.
The warning appears once per launch and is only counted after you dismiss it.
The popup is suppressed while the app is loading and during onboarding so it won’t interrupt setup.
The alert offers an “I’m a Tester” dismiss button and a “How to Return to Main” link to documentation.

includedPullRequests.title: Show Dev Branch Warning Popup
includedPullRequests.body: ## Summary Adds a startup warning, modelled on Loop's dev-branch alert, shown once per launch when the build's branch is anything other than main. > [!IMPORTANT] > Blocked by an update to TrioDocs. > See `trio-docs` PR https://github.com/nightscout/trio-docs/pull/257 The branch is already recorded in `BuildDetails.plist` by `capture-build-details.sh` and read back through `BuildDetails.trioBranch`, so no new build-time plumbing is needed. Wording adapts: the dev branch is named directly, anything else names the branch that was actually built. Suppressed while Core Data is loading and during onboarding. The scene phase hook alone cannot carry the warning on a cold launch, because the scene is already active by the time Core Data finishes, so it is also triggered as the loading screen gives way to the app. Compile with `DEV_BRANCH_WARNING_DISABLED` to suppress it. The project-level Debug configuration hardcoded `SWIFT_ACTIVE_COMPILATION_CONDITIONS` without `$(inherited)`, which silently discarded the flag for Debug builds; adding `$(inherited)` makes `ConfigOverride.xcconfig` behave the same in Debug and Release. Browser builds can set the repository variable `DEV_BRANCH_WARNING_DISABLED` instead. `AppVersionChecker` presents from the same root view controller on the same scene phase change, and UIKit drops a second presentation silently. showAlert now skips when another alert is already showing and reports whether it appeared, so its callers no longer burn their 24 hour and 2 week throttles on an alert that was never displayed. ### Screenshots | ☀ feature branch | ☀ dev | ☾ feature branch | ☾ dev | |--------|--------|--------|--------| | | | | |

Browser builds can set the repository variable `DEV_BRANCH_WARNING_DISABLED` instead. `AppVersionChecker` presents from the same root view controller on the same scene phase change, and UIKit drops a second presentation silently. showAlert now skips when another alert is already showing and reports whether it appeared, so its callers no longer burn their 24 hour and 2 week throttles on an alert that was never displayed. ### Screenshots | ☀ feature branch | ☀ dev | ☾ feature branch | ☾ dev | |--------|--------|--------|--------| | | | | |

highlights.title: Fix CI unit tests and speed up workflows
changes: Continuous integration unit tests now run more reliably in CI.
Golden-file comparisons no longer fail due to time zone mismatches.
An insulin IOB unit test was fixed to use the expected ascending treatment order.

includedPullRequests.title: Fix CI Unit Tests
includedPullRequests.body:
## Summary

Trio dev’s CI unit tests have been failing since #1377 merged (it was merged with both checks already failing). Both jobs fail, for three independent reasons.

Reference run: https://github.com/nightscout/Trio/actions/runs/31322045618

1. Algorithm package no longer compiles. AlgorithmPackage/OpenAPSSwiftTests is a symlink to TrioTests/OpenAPSSwiftTests, so the new Parity/ files joined the SPM test target. They throw TestError, declared in TrioTests/TestError.swift one directory up, outside the symlink: 
* ParityHarness.swift:33:19: error: cannot find 'TestError' in scope
* ParityScenarios.swift:249:19: error: cannot find 'TestError' in scope
* Replaced with a local ParityError. Also excluded Parity/goldens from the target. They are read via #filePath, and SwiftPM warned about 70 undeclared files on every build.

2. Test runner crash from the iobTotal precondition. IobCalculation.prepare now binary-searches the DIA cutoff and asserts its treatments are sorted ascending. IobTotalTests."should ignore future treatments" passes them descending, so both jobs abort mid-run: Trio/IobCalculation.swift:141: Assertion failed: iobTotal treatments must be sorted ascending
Every production caller feeds calcTempTreatments output, which is sorted, so the test input was the wrong side of the contract. Reordered; the test still asserts the future bolus is ignored.

3. Parity goldens only compare on a Europe/Berlin machine. ParityEnv.pinned sets NSTimeZone.default, which moves Calendar.current but not TimeZone.current — and TimeZone.current is what WallClock reads. On the GMT runner the pipeline ran in GMT against goldens recorded in Europe/Berlin: `Expectation failed: (TimeZone.current.identifier → "GMT") == (ParityEnv.timeZoneIdentifier → "Europe/Berlin”)`.
This led to 126 issues in OpenAPSSwift golden parity, 9288 in Wall clock parity. The pin now repoints the process time zone (setenv / tzset / resetSystemTimeZone), which both APIs honour. This was invisible locally because the goldens were authored in the pinned zone.
 
Also: QuickPickTreatmentsTests.swift is rewritten by the SwiftFormat build phase, which CI reports as Uncommitted change detected. This PR commits a linting fix.

includedPullRequests.title: Fix duplicate remote meal being re-stored on replay
includedPullRequests.body:
## Summary

The guard in `handleMealCommand` that rejects a remote meal when newer carb entries already exist never actually aborts the handler. Its `return` sits inside a nested `Task {}` inside `taskContext.perform {}`, so it only exits that closure. The handler logs "Command rejected" and then stores the carbs anyway.

This computes the fetch result via `await taskContext.perform { ... }` returning a `Bool` and guards from the handler itself, so the rejection stops storage.

## Background

Noticed while running Trio with LoopFollow remote control for our young daughter. If a meal command is delivered twice (APNs redelivery, or a caregiver resend after an unclear failure), the duplicate carbs are stored and dosed for, while the log claims the command was rejected.

I'm @justmaier on the Trio Discord if it's easier to discuss there.

Fixes #1348

includedPullRequests.title: Bump OmnipodKit to 792dc19
includedPullRequests.body:
Moves the `OmnipodKit` submodule to the current tip of [loopandlearn/OmnipodKit `dev`](https://github.com/loopandlearn/OmnipodKit/tree/dev). Follow-up to #1380.

`e31a8d1` → `792dc19`

### What's included

https://github.com/loopandlearn/OmnipodKit/pull/128:
`4162807` Fix re-entrant `managerQueue` deadlock surfacing a pod alert from an advert

`surfacePodConditionAndQuiet` runs on `managerQueue` (from `centralManager didDiscover`) and called `omnipodDidDetectAlert` inline. The host handles that synchronously via `getPodStatus` → `runSession` → `bleRunSession` → `peripheralManager(forIdentifier:)`, which does `managerQueue.sync` — a sync-to-self deadlock. It fired on a fresh launch when a DASH pod advertised a fault/alert transition before any connection had established `BlePodComms.manager`. The fix dispatches the delegate notification off `managerQueue`; alarm-scan quieting stays on it.

includedPullRequests.title: Plot Projected COB Decay in Home View Chart
includedPullRequests.body: ## Summary > [!IMPORTANT] > Depends on #1382 — this branch is based on it, so the diff shows its commits until it merges. Will be rebased onto dev afterwards; only the last commit is new here. Twin of #1382's IOB projection, for carbs: the COB pane now shows a dashed orange decay curve of forecasted carb absorption from "now" into the future. ### Decay Calculation The series is derived inside forecastCOB from the exact carb-impact terms that already makes up the COB-specific forecast. The linearly decaying observed carb impact plus the remaining-carbs triangle, divided by CSF, gives grams absorbed per 5-minute step, 48 values make up a 4 hours forecast. Subtracting from mealCOB (floored at 0) yields remaining COB per step. TODO: In a follow-up PR, refactor this to core data so per-cycle outputs become replayable. ### Additional Notes This is oref's own (crude) absorption model (linear carb impact decay and “triangle”-like instant decay, with a 30 g/hr cap), recomputed each cycle from observed deviations. The curve subsequently reshapes between algorithm runs. It shows what the algorithm currently “believes", not necessarily physiological prediction.

includedPullRequests.title: Fix IOB area stacking + plot projected IOB decay
includedPullRequests.body: ## Summary ### Fix: IOB shading rendered above the COB area **Reported on Discord:** IOB plot fill was drawn above the COB chart. **Reason:** The COB/IOB pane draws its marks with fixed styles and explicit series: identities (introduced with the home-refactor chart rework). Swift Charts stacks AreaMarks that share an x value by default, and series: does not opt out of stacking — so the IOB area was offset upward by the COB value whenever COB > 0, floating above the COB area instead of hugging the IOB line. Line marks never stack, which is why only the shading was wrong. Fixed by declaring stacking: .unstacked on both area marks. ### Feature: projected active insulin in the COB/IOB pane oref already computes a full IOB projection every loop cycle, up to 48 points at 5 minute cadence, 4 hours ahead (the same array whose activity values feed the glucose forecasting in determine basal). Trio already persists this to `monitor/iob.json` each loop cycle. This PR surfaces it: - `IOBService` (which already watches the iob file) exposes the array as `iobProjection` - `HomeStateModel` mirrors it alongside `currentIOB` - the COB/IOB pane draws it as a dashed line with a faint area from "now" into the future, anchored at the newest determination's `deliverAt` - Any stale projection (older than newest determination) renders nothing, and points beyond the chart window are dropped Tested in the simulator with CGM + pump sims: carbs on board plus SMB-driven IOB confirm the shading now stays inside the IOB line with COB present, and the dashed decay curve renders from the current-time marker to the chart edge. ### Screenshots |

highlights.title: Faster algorithm with identical dosing
changes: The insulin-calculation pipeline runs about twice as fast in testing.
Dosing decisions are unchanged and match previous outputs exactly.
New automated parity tests record and compare exact outputs across many scenarios.
Calculation-heavy scenarios use less CPU time, improving responsiveness.

Trio now uses a newer OmnipodKit version that includes this connectivity fix.

## oref-swift performance pass

Speeds up the native oref pipeline ~2× with **bit-identical dosing behavior**. Every change is either a pure refactor (same values, same rounding, same operation order) or verified byte-for-byte by golden tests recorded on unmodified code.

  ### What changed

  - **Golden parity harness** — 14 scenarios (low/high BG, active COB, temp target, override, dynamic ISF log/sigmoid, autosens both directions, suspend/resume, dense 24 h history, stale BG, DST/winter clock) with committed byte-exact goldens for every pipeline stage (profile, autosens, meal, IOB, determination incl. the full `reason` string). Re-record with `TEST_RUNNER_TRIO_RECORD_GOLDENS=1`.
  - **Cache ISF and basal schedules in hot loops** — the per-bucket rebuild+sort of the ISF/basal schedules (autosens simulation, COB detection, temp-basal splitting) is hoisted into prepared, sorted lookup tables built once per loop.
  - **Hoist invariant curve constants out of IOB loop** — the exponential-curve constants and duplicated `exp`/`pow` work move out of the per-treatment kernel; identical left-associated arithmetic, so results are bit-identical.
  - **Reuse prepared IOB inputs across time points** — treatments are preprocessed once (insulin pre-converted, nil-insulin events dropped) and each `iobTotal` call selects its window via binary search over the sorted array instead of a full-array filter.
  - **Share treatment computation across autosens runs** — the 8 h and 24 h autosens runs and the per-carb-entry COB loop no longer rebuild identical intermediate arrays.
  - **Compute wall-clock time without Calendar** — `Calendar.dateComponents` is replaced by a UTC-offset computation cached between DST transitions. This is the one deliberate exception to keeping the algorithm stateless (it is only a cache, marked as such in the code); a dedicated parity test sweeps DST transitions and sub-second boundaries against `Calendar`.

Transcribed and de-identified. I've mapped the three testers to **A / B / C**, keeping the same letter for the before/after pair so the optimization comparison stays intact (A un-opt → A opt is the same setup; B and C are the other two datasets).

highlights.title: Add Today stats interval
changes: A new 'Today' time interval is added for statistics, showing the current calendar day from midnight until now.
Insulin and Meal stats now default to the 'Today' interval and show the current day's data.
Charts and axis labels show hourly granularity for 'Today' (and Day), and scrolling aligns to hours or midnight.
Averages and totals update from the visible hourly range when viewing 'Today' instead of using daily caches.

highlights.title: Home screen redesign (Layout v2)
changes: The home screen now uses fixed-height zones so the chart is the only flexible area.
Updated visual style and glass UI refresh the header, panels, bottom banner, and tab bar.
A single multi-use bottom panel shows the highest-priority state and allows tap-through actions while keeping stats in.
The glucose chart is now interactive with drag, momentum panning, pinch-to-zoom, double-tap presets, and press-and-hold.

highlights.title: Interactive home chart with pinch, pan, and scrub
changes: The main Home chart is now draggable and pans smoothly with momentum when you swipe it.
You can pinch to zoom the chart between short and long windows and double-tap to cycle zoom presets.
Press-and-hold on the chart shows a selection popover so you can inspect and scrub exact values.
Pulling the dashboard down forces a refresh/loop and shows an inline refresh indicator.
Basal bars now hang from the top of their pane and basal schedule visuals update after profile changes.

highlights.title: 72-hour chart and smoother zoom
changes: The home chart now shows up to 72 hours of history when opened.
Charts render only the visible time span plus padding to keep panning and zooming responsive.
You can pinch-zoom in to 1 hour, with smoother previews that snap to stable zoom steps.
When auto-following, the current glucose reading stays visible at tight zoom levels.
The Time in Range banner now shows 'today', and midnight x-axis ticks include day labels.

highlights.title: Multi-use home panel replaces stats banner
changes: The home stats banner is replaced by one multi-use panel that defaults to showing real time-in-range stats.
Panel banners respond to taps across their full area.
If notifications are disabled the panel shows a critical warning and opens the app Settings when tapped.
If CGM data is stale the panel shows a No Recent Glucose banner that opens a manual glucose entry sheet.
If the pump clock differs or Max IOB is zero the panel shows warnings that open pump setup or deep-link to the Max IOB.

highlights.title: Immediate stop of crash uploads on opt-out
changes: When you turn off Diagnostics, any crash reports waiting to be sent are deleted and stop uploading.
After opting out, the app no longer starts Firebase services so no new diagnostic data is re‑queued or sent.
Turning Diagnostics back on re-enables Firebase and allows diagnostic reporting to resume immediately.

items.title: Home dashboard zoning with fixed slots
changes: Home dashboard now reserves fixed-height slots for the header, meal row, and bottom controls.
The chart is the only flexible area and fills the remaining vertical space.
Bottom controls are placed in the safe area so the tab bar cannot cover them.
Banners, badges, and the bolus bar no longer trigger layout reflow, and dashboard size is capped to avoid overflow on大型.

changes: Home header and panels were reorganized into a new glass-style layout with pump and loop panels.
A tappable Time‑in‑Range (TIR) stats banner was added under the adjustment panel and opens statistics when tapped.
The adjustments panel now shows remaining-time progress bars for overrides and temp targets, supports concurrent split‑.
bars, and the whole panel responds to full taps.
Meal row now shows an alarms pill that displays a snooze countdown and opens snooze controls when tapped.

The arc starts full and empties back toward 12 o'clock during warmup, grace, and lifetime.

includedPullRequests.title: Home Layout v2
includedPullRequests.body:
## Summary

This integrates **Home Layout v2**, a fully refactored version of Trio's home screen as tracked in #1350, into `dev`. It brings in the seven-part stacked series that was developed and reviewed on the `feat/home-refactor` branch (#1326–#1332):

- **Zoning (#1326)** — fixed-height zones (header / meal row / bottom controls) with the chart as the only flexible zone. Bottom controls sit in a `safeAreaInset` so the tab bar can't cover them, and dashboard type size is capped, so badges, banners, and the bolus indicator no longer reflow the layout.
- **Layout rework (#1327)** — restyled header, panels, meal row, and the bottom stats banner.
- **Multi-use bottom panel (#1328)** — one slot where the highest-priority state wins: notifications-disabled → pump time mismatch → stale/missing CGM → Max IOB = 0 → today's statistics as the default face. Replaces the old stack of competing banners and gives each attention-state a consistent, non-blocking tap-through action. Statistics stay reachable via a fallback item in the History toolbar.
- **Interactive chart (#1329)** — draggable panning with momentum, pinch-to-zoom (1–24 h), double-tap presets, press-and-hold scrub-to-inspect, and pull-down-to-force-loop, replacing the fixed time-interval buttons.
- **72 h history (#1330)** — windowed rendering draws only the visible span plus padding, so the longer history doesn't cost per-frame layout.
- **Sensor lifecycle arc (#1331)** — the CGM arc now counts down toward 12 o'clock (warm-up, grace, lifetime) instead of filling up.
- **Liquid Glass (#1332)** — turns off UIKit compatibility mode and adopts real iOS 26 glass (`GlassChrome`) with a pre-26 material fallback, plus a glass tab bar with a centered treatment button.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> This is a UI / layout / rendering change only — it does **not** touch the algorithm, dosing, or the Core Data predicates that feed oref.

## Additional Notes

The work here was already reviewed and merged part-by-part in #1326–#1332, each of which was independently shippable. This PR is the integration merge of that series onto `dev`. The commit history preserves the per-part boundaries if one wants to step through it.

includedPullRequests.title: Stop Crashlytics Uploads Immediately After Diagnostics Opt-Out
includedPullRequests.body:
`setCrashlyticsCollectionEnabled(false)` only gates future events. The FirebaseSessions event GoogleDataTransport already queued stays on disk and GDT retries it for seven days, so firebaselogging-pa.googleapis.com still shows up in App Privacy Report minutes after opting out.

Route both call sites through `CrashReportingGate: purge` GDT's store when a Trio user opts out, and skip `FirebaseApp.configure()` on any later launches so nothing can re-queue or upload queued sessions. 

Trio’s opt-out-by-default stays unchanged.

Fixes #1372.

includedPullRequests.body:
NOTE: We might want a feature branch instead of merging to dev

This PR adds the Accu-Chek SmartGuide CGM to Trio.

### Why?

The short answer would be: The more, the better.

This CGM is generally covered by insurance and because of the missing pump integration an interesting option to attract new users.

### What is the Accu-Chek SmartGuide?

Link: https://www.accu-chek.co.uk/products/smartguide-cgm

The Accu-Chek CGM is a 14-day CGM made by Roche.
It comes with its own app and a prediction app, no direct integrations with a pump possible.

This CGM needs to be calibrated twice at the beginning of its lifespan, at the 12h mark and 30 min after.
The first calibration will stay open until you enter the calibration (possible via Trio or the official app).
The second calibration needs to be done after 30min of the first calibration and before 2.5hr.
If you miss this calibration, this process needs to be re-done.

**Linked PR:** 
https://github.com/nightscout/trio-docs/pull/247

includedPullRequests.title: Add AccuChek SmartGuide CGM to dev
includedPullRequests.body:
## Summary

This PR adds the AccuChek SmartGuide CGM to Trio `dev`.

The Accu-Chek CGM is a 14-day CGM made by Roche.
It comes with its own app and a prediction app, no direct integrations with a pump possible.

This CGM needs to be calibrated twice at the beginning of its lifespan, at the 12h mark and 30 min after.
The first calibration will stay open until you enter the calibration (possible via Trio or the official app).
The second calibration needs to be done after 30min of the first calibration and before 2.5hr.
If you miss this calibration, this process needs to be re-done.

## Additional Notes

This CGM and its Trio driver has been used by multiple users over the span of at least one sensor up to multiple months. We are moving ahead in adding it to Trio `dev` to make it available for more users and potential testing.

includedPullRequests.title: Bump LoopKit and OmnipodKit, Streamline BLE Heartbeat Handling with Loop
includedPullRequests.body:
## Summary

This PR updates pump BLE heartbeat support so the pump can better wake the app when the CGM can't do so on its own, mirroring Loop's approach.

- Bump LoopKit and OmnipodKit: LoopKit moves to the trio tip with the LoopKit#599 dev backport (`PumpHeartbeatRequest`, `setBLEHeartbeatRequest`, `expectedGlucoseSampleInterval`). OmnipodKit moves to the ble-heartbeat tip, picking up pairing fixes (#116), stale-target advance (#117), and the next-dev heartbeat backport (#118).
- Wire pump heartbeat to CGM schedule: A `PumpHeartbeatRequest` is pushed after each stored reading batch, re-applied when the pump manager is set, and refreshed on foreground, mirroring Loop's `updatePumpManagerBLEHeartbeatPreference`.
- Guard pump heartbeat on CGM capability: A pump BLE heartbeat is only requested when the active glucose source can't wake the app itself (non-plugin sources and plugins without `providesBLEHeartbeat`). This fixes the hardcoded `true` in `pumpManagerMustProvideBLEHeartbeat` and retracts the request when switching to a heartbeat-capable CGM.

highlights.title: Serialize Tidepool uploads
changes: Tidepool uploads are now serialized so only one upload runs at a time.
Rapid triggers for the same upload type are coalesced so the same data is not uploaded twice.
Hung or lost upload calls now time out and are logged instead of silently stalling later uploads.
Tidepool upload log messages are corrected and are now labelled [Service] for clarity.

sources.title: nightscout/Trio#1321: Fix Tidepool uploads with serialization

includedPullRequests.title: Fix Tidepool uploads with serialization
includedPullRequests.body:
Fixes #1235

## Problem

Trio fired Tidepool uploads concurrently and unserialized: each pipeline's trigger (glucose, carbs, dose, settings observers) independently spawned a `Task` into the shared TidepoolKit `TAPI` actor, so several uploads were routinely in flight at once.

When the OAuth access token expired, multiple in-flight requests each passed `session.shouldRefresh()` and called `refreshSession()` in parallel, reusing the single-use rotating refresh token. That race corrupted the session; subsequent upload completions never fired, so uploads stopped silently with nothing logged.

Confirmed from the issue logs in #1235: last Tidepool success at 01:50:06, zero Tidepool errors after, app running continuously to 07:33; at 07:31 a dose reached the upload path but its completion never returned.

Nightscout uploads were unaffected (separate manager), and Loop avoids the bug by funneling uploads through one serialized `RemoteDataServicesManager` cycle.

## Fix

A new `TidepoolUploadSerializer` actor routes every upload (glucose, carbs, dose/pump events, settings, deletes) through a single chain so only one network request is in flight at a time. This guarantees at most one session refresh, eliminating the concurrent-refresh race, and a wedged request now resolves to a logged failure instead of silently stalling every later upload forever.

Design points (several adopted from the Nightscout upload serializer in #1290):

- **Run-time fetching + coalescing.** Each pipeline's operation fetches its pending rows (or rebuilds its payload) inside the serialized run rather than at trigger time. Two triggers firing close together previously could both snapshot the same unmarked rows and upload them twice; now the second coalesces into a follow-up that re-fetches after the first run marked its rows. A trigger burst costs at most one waiting run per pipeline. Delete pipelines carry unique payloads and never coalesce.
- **Per-chunk marking.** Chunked uploads mark only the chunk that succeeded as uploaded, instead of marking the full batch after the first chunk.
- **Watchdog.** A wall-clock watchdog abandons the chain when its head operation exceeds 10 minutes (e.g. the app was suspended mid-request and the completion was lost). It's checked at each enqueue and on app foreground — the reliable recovery points while the pipeline itself is stalled. Abandoning bumps a generation counter; operations re-check it between network calls so an orphaned chain can't fire requests alongside its replacement.
- **Timeout backstop.** `awaitUpload` bridges TidepoolKit's completion-based calls into async/await with a 120s timeout, so a call that never invokes its completion resolves to a logged `.timedOut` failure instead of suspending the chain forever.
- **QoS.** Chain tasks run at a pinned `.utility` rather than inheriting the caller's priority — `.utility` stays scheduled during background execution windows (`.background` would not), without running network uploads at UI priority.

## Also in this PR

- **Log fixes.** Tidepool upload results were logged as `[Nightscout]`, making Tidepool failures look like Nightscout activity; they're now tagged `[Service]`, and carbs-delete results are worded distinctly from carbs uploads.

## Tests

`TidepoolUploadSerializerTests` covers:

- Operations run strictly one at a time, in enqueue order (peak concurrency stays at 1).
- A request burst for a coalescing pipeline folds into exactly one follow-up run; delete pipelines never coalesce; coalescing is keyed per pipeline.
- The watchdog abandons a wedged chain so later uploads run again, clears coalescing state so the pipeline can run on the fresh chain, and leaves an idle chain alone; an abandoned operation sees a stale generation and bails out, and its late completion can't corrupt the fresh chain's watchdog state.
- `awaitUpload` returns the completion's result, resolves to `.timedOut` when the completion never fires, and ignores a late completion after the timeout.

includedPullRequests.title: improved Browser Build, update fastlane
includedPullRequests.body:
## Purpose

1. Update fastlane to same version as LoopWorkspace
2. Adopt the LoopFollow method of explicitly skipping an automatic build on weeks when no build is completed (details below), and update Xcode version to 26.5, same as is used in LoopWorkspace

## Details

The scheduled weekly run checks for new commits and only builds when something changed (or when the monthly forced build is due). When there is nothing to build, the build jobs are skipped and the run still completes with a green check — indistinguishable at a glance from a successful build. Users who rely on the green status can believe they have a fresh build even when their last real build attempt failed.

Copied the change from https://github.com/loopandlearn/LoopFollow/pull/705. See that PR for more information.

Status semantics after this change:

green — a new build was made and uploaded to TestFlight
cancelled (grey) — the repository was already up to date, nothing was built
red — a build was attempted and failed

includedPullRequests.title: Do not enact a meal's explicit bolus when the meal is rejected
includedPullRequests.body:
## Summary

For a remote meal command with `bolusAmount`, the `.meal` dispatch calls `handleMealCommand` and then enacts the bolus whenever `bolusAmount != nil`. Since `handleMealCommand` reports validation failures by logging and returning (it doesn't throw), a rejected meal still delivers its bolus. Carbs over the configured max is the easiest way to hit it.

This moves the bolus decision inside `handleMealCommand`, after the meal has validated and stored, so an early return also suppresses the bolus. The standalone `bolus` command is unchanged.

## Background

The max-carbs check exists to catch fat-fingered remote entries, but today it rejects the carbs and delivers the insulin anyway. The caregiver sees a rejection notification and has no reason to think a bolus went through. Found while reviewing the remote meal path for our daughter's caregiver setup.

I'm @justmaier on the Trio Discord if it's easier to discuss there.

Fixes #1349

includedPullRequests.title: Preserve non-manager CGM lifecycle state on Home
includedPullRequests.body:
## Summary

Preserve CGM lifecycle and status state published by non-manager `GlucoseSource` implementations on the Home screen.

This supports non-direct CGM connections such as xDrip4iOS AppGroup, where Trio receives lifecycle information through the glucose source rather than through a native `CGMManager`.

## Why

Home has a periodic refresh that re-reads CGM lifecycle and status information. Before this change, that refresh only used a native `CGMManager`, with a simulator fallback. Non-manager sources can publish lifecycle and status through `GlucoseSource`, but the refresh path cleared those values because no native manager exists.

The Home view also used `cgmSensorExpiresAt` as part of the sensor ring display gate. Non-manager sources can provide valid lifecycle progress without a manager-derived expiration date, so Home now tracks when progress came from a source publisher and allows that source-origin progress to render.

## Changes

- Preserve source-published lifecycle and status during the Home refresh for non-manager glucose sources.
- Track whether lifecycle progress came from a non-manager source.
- Allow source-origin lifecycle progress to show the sensor ring without requiring a native manager expiration date.
- Keep native `CGMManager` and simulator paths separate.

## Compatibility

This remains fully backward compatible with xDrip4iOS versions before v7. Legacy AppGroup payloads that only write the top-level readings array continue to publish nil lifecycle and status state, so Trio does not fabricate a sensor ring.

Native CGM managers still refresh directly from `cgmLifecycleProgress` and `cgmStatusHighlight`. Native sources with `cgmSensorExpiresAt` still use the existing 48 hour display gate. Simulator behavior remains special-cased.

## Testing

Validated on-device with xDrip4iOS AppGroup data from the forthcoming xdripswift v7 update:
- [JohanDegraeve/xdripswift#730](https://github.com/JohanDegraeve/xdripswift/pull/730)

Tested cases:
- lifecycle ring displays from source-published state
- ring remains visible across Home refresh ticks
- legacy and no-lifecycle payloads do not fabricate ring state
- soon-to-expire `maxSensorDays` cases display correctly
- expired `maxSensorDays` cases display correctly

includedPullRequests.title: Make Watch-app & -complication follow ConfigOverride.xcconfig
includedPullRequests.body:
The main app name can be overriden by either changing it in XCode or, easier for all future use, put an entry in ConfigOverride.xcconfig to overrule it.

However, this currently only affects Trio's main target as the rest is hardcoded to "Trio" within this file instead of referencing $(APP_DISPLAY_NAME). So the Watch app and Complication get set to "Trio" and ignores the ConfigOverride value.

This minor change makes XCode also look at ConfigOverride.xcconfig for the Watch and Watch Complication targets. When the file isn't present or does not contain a line to override APP_DISPLAY_NAME, it defaults back to "Trio" as defined in Config.xcconfig (it follows what's in that file when ConfigOverride.xcconfig isn't present or lacks the key). 

See comments for an additional remark.

includedPullRequests.title: Fix temp target presets showing up in the main chart
includedPullRequests.body:
Fixes #1324

Saving a new Temp Target as a preset made it show up in the main chart even though it was never activated. The chart's fetch predicate freezes its date anchors when it is built and only re-anchors when the app comes to the foreground, so a fresh preset (date now, enabled false) matched the clause meant for scheduled temp targets. The same stale anchor also kept a cancelled temp target's full bar on the chart until the app was backgrounded.

Presets are now excluded from the scheduled clause, and the fetched results are filtered again with a fresh date before they reach the chart. Added tests covering the predicate and the visibility rules.

includedPullRequests.title: Make bolus-in-progress card in Treatments view more reliable
includedPullRequests.body:
Some manual boluses left a bolusing card stuck at 0% in the Treatments view that blocked further boluses and could not be dismissed until the app was restarted (#1308).

The card was gated on bolusStatus, which mirrors the pump's reported bolusState and can stay at inProgress after delivery has finished. Since bolusTrigger now retains that value, the card resurfaced once a new amount was entered, and the X could not clear it because there was no active bolus to cancel.

Gate the card on bolusProgress instead, the local dose reporter signal that clears reliably and that the Home view already uses, keeping the initiating state so the pre-delivery view still shows.

includedPullRequests.title: Fix duplicate Nightscout treatment uploads by serializing per-pipeline runs
includedPullRequests.body:
## Problem

Trio occasionally uploads the same treatment to Nightscout twice — most visibly Exercise entries for overrides enacted via Shortcuts or remote commands. Reproduced with an APNS remote command producing two documents with millisecond-identical `created_at` and consecutive Mongo `_id`s, i.e. two near-simultaneous POSTs:

- Enacting an override via App Intents / remote control triggers uploads twice: the Core Data save fires the upload pipeline, and `.willUpdateOverrideConfiguration` fires a direct, unthrottled upload. Both fetch the same rows still marked `isUploadedToNS == false` before either has marked them uploaded.
- Nightscout's treatment upsert is a non-atomic find-then-insert (no unique index), so concurrent identical POSTs both insert. Sequential re-posts are deduped server-side; only concurrent ones slip through. (API v3 has the same race, so switching API versions wouldn't help.)
- The 2s throttle didn't prevent this: it only spaced out task starts within one trigger path, never waited for the previous upload to finish, and with `latest: false` silently dropped triggers arriving inside its window. Carb edits had a third, entirely unthrottled path (`HistoryStateModel` calls `uploadCarbs()` directly).

## Solution

Replace the per-pipeline subject/throttle machinery with `NightscoutUploadSerializer`, an actor that coalesces and serializes upload runs per pipeline:

- An idle pipeline starts a run immediately; while a run is in flight, exactly one follow-up is queued and further requests coalesce into it.
- No two runs of a pipeline ever overlap: a follow-up re-fetches only after the previous run marked its rows uploaded, so it finds nothing left to send. Queued runs double as retry attempts after network failures.
- The upload routine is provided once at init; `request(_:)`/`run(_:)` take only the pipeline, so every entry point (Core Data triggers, App Intents, remote control, direct calls) is covered with no call-site changes.
- App Intents semantics are preserved: `uploadOverrides()`/`uploadTempTargets()` are awaitable, so `.didUpdateOverrideConfiguration` still posts only after the upload attempt finished.

## Benefits

- No more duplicate treatments, regardless of how many trigger paths fire for the same change.
- Uploads start immediately — the fixed 2-second throttle delay is gone.
- No dropped triggers (the old throttle discarded a second change arriving within 2 s; it stayed unuploaded until the next unrelated trigger).
- `uploadDeviceStatus()` no longer throws; its only caller was the deleted pipeline dispatch, and errors are logged in `performUpload(for:)`.

Unit tests cover the serializer: no overlap under concurrency, queued-run ordering, burst coalescing into a single follow-up, completion semantics, and pipeline independence.

includedPullRequests.title: [Part 5 of 6] Remove JSON encoding for pump events
includedPullRequests.body:
This commit removes the old:
* CoreData -> DTOs -> JSON string -> [PumpHistoryEvent]

pipeline and replaces it with a direct pipeline:
* CoreData -> [PumpHistoryEvent]

The result of the two pipelines should be identical, except for the
handling of the subtype tempType of temp basal events, which we
nullify if we get an unrecognized string vs crashing as the old
pipeline would. This change is safe as Trio only ever records
"absolute" types and the value is copied but never actually used by
the algorithm.

includedPullRequests.title: Fix Temp Target and Override delete confirmation auto-dismissing
includedPullRequests.body:
Fixes #1314

Deleting a Temp Target or Override preset by swiping was unreliable. The delete confirmation only appeared for a moment before auto-dismissing, so the preset often couldn't be deleted.

The confirmation dialog was attached to the ForEach inside the List and driven by two state variables set at the same time, which made it dismiss itself. Reworked it to match the History screen: a single optional drives the dialog via presenting:, attached once to the view. Applied to both Temp Targets and Overrides.

includedPullRequests.body:
This commit is the last part of our removal of the JSON conversion we
used to do when we ran the oref algorithm using Javascript. In this
commit, we remove the OpenAPSSwift file and just call the underlying
algorithm functions directly from OpenAPS.

One change in functionality is that we expose raw DeterminationError
messages instead of catching them and converting them to APSError
exceptions with a generic "No determination error" error
message. These exception messages will be user visible when they
happen.

includedPullRequests.title: Remove explicit allowsConstrainedNetworkAccess setting for Nightscout uploads
includedPullRequests.body:
## Summary

This PR removes the explicit `allowsConstrainedNetworkAccess` setting from all Nightscout upload requests.

This restores the default `URLRequest` behavior and lets iOS decide how constrained network access should be handled according to the user's system settings.

## Background

While investigating intermittent Nightscout upload failures, repeated `Constrained path prohibited` errors were observed in the logs. This PR follows the review discussion and removes the explicit flag instead of overriding the system default.

includedPullRequests.title: Core Data Performance Improvements, Fixes and Adjustments
includedPullRequests.body:
**Core Data Context Rework**
Eliminates long-lived shared `NSManagedObjectContext` instances across all storages and service classes which was the reason for inconsistencies in the synchronization of our background contexts and probably also the root cause for the crash that was solved differently with one of my previous PRs #1100. Each data operation now creates a fresh task context via `CoreDataStack.shared.newTaskContext()`, preventing cross-context data races and stale object access. Every background context now is only active for a special task and it has the latest data from the `PersistentStore`. This is done similarly in Apples Earthquakes Sample: https://github.com/TomaszLizer/Apple-Earthquakes/

Those changes need to be tested thoroughly. I am testing it on myself for about 2 months now without any problems. But in theory I could have accidentally introduced a wrong `NSManagedObjectContext` access in a class that I simply don't use. This should be deteced via our `ConcurrencyDebug` flag though which then makes the app crash. So be aware of that.

 **N+1 Query Elimination**
 Adds `relationshipKeyPathsForPrefetching` for bolus/tempBasal on all `PumpEventStored` fetches (`OpenAPS`, `APSManager`, `WatchManager`, `GarminManager`)and `forecastValues` on `OrefDetermination` fetches. Eliminates hundreds of individual `WHERE Z_PK = ?` round-trips per Loop that I could identify in the SQLDebug logs. When we were fetching a pump event with its bolus relationship for example the relationships don't get loaded automatically, but instead created as a fault. So when we were doing 1 query only to iterate over the items to get its bolus property after that this was unefficient as this would fire several faults. `relationshipKeyPathsForPrefetching` gets rid of this as the bolus property is now already in the context cache after the first query.

**TDD Aggregate Optimization**
Replaces full ZTDDStored row loads (up to 1,041 rows) in `calculateWeightedAverage` with a single SQL aggregate query `(SELECT total(), COUNT())` — reducing fetch time from ~6 ms to ~0.8 ms per call.

**Carb/FPU & Determination Prefetch**
 Adds `SELF IN` batch-prefetch hop for CarbEntryStored and OrefDetermination in the Home state model to prevent N+1 faults during `getNSManagedObject` materialization on the view context.

**NSFetchedResultsController migration**
New NSFetchedResultsControllerDelegate plus migration of HomeStateModel, TreatmentsStateModel, NightscoutManager, TidepoolManager, and HealthKitManager to FRCs bound to the viewContext, replacing the previous objectID/publisher logic.

**History-sourced change feed (CoreDataObserver.swift)**
The hand-rolled `changedObjectsOnManagedObjectContextDidSavePublisher` (based on `NSManagedObjectContextDidSave`) is replaced by `CoreDataStack.entityChangePublisher`, sourced from persistent history. This now also captures batch operations and cross-process changes.

**New dedup logic in `PumpHistoryStorage`**
The new dedup key combines `timestamp` AND `type` so that a bolus and temp basal event can coexist at the same time. Also add a unique constraint that ensures this behaviour.

includedPullRequests.title: Fix Spurious Pump Alerts
includedPullRequests.body:
## Summary

The alerting rework routes pump-thrown alerts through the LoopKit protocol as intended. Tapping a notification calls acknowledgeAlert on the PM, no auto-ack anywhere. But it missed one spot: dismissing the in-app banner (and swiping away the UN) routed to snooze only, so the ack was never sent to the PM. With the app foregrounded, a pod alert could stay unacknowledged on the pod indefinitely unless the user also tapped the notification, leaving pods beeping on their repeat schedule (15 min expiration reminder, hourly low reservoir/expired) and alerts stuck as unacknowledged.

Dismissal is the user's response, so requestSnooze now also forwards the ack to the issuing device manager via acknowledgeOnDevice(), extracted from handleAcknowledgement. The forward is guarded on a registered AlertResponder – only device managers register (currently just the pump manager) – so Trio-internal alerts (glucose for Libre 3 and other CGms that require it, not-looping, algorithm) are unaffected, and PMs with no-op ack's (Medtrum, Dana, Minimed) see no behavior change.

User-facing behavior is unchanged: swipe/tap away still auto-snoozes for 15 min and dismisses both presentations, **but** pump alerts are now properly acknowledged at the PM layer (e.g. AcknowledgeAlerts reaches the pod and silences its beeps).

Fixes #1135.

includedPullRequests.body:
(duplicate of #1206)
(provided feedback from previous PR https://github.com/nightscout/Trio/pull/1206#issuecomment-4702981172)

includedPullRequests.title: Refactor Trio Alert/Notification Handling – Prepare O5 and Libre 3/3+ Integration [1/3]
includedPullRequests.body: ## Summary Refactors Trio's entire alert / notification handling. Routes all device + glucose alerts through a single `TrioAlertManager` (serves as LoopKit `AlertIssuer`/`AlertResponder`), introduces a user-configurable glucose alarm list (LoopFollow-style), tiered device-alarm list, a shared Day/Night window, and unifies snooze handling across phone / watch / banner / lock-screen quick-action. **Basic functionality:** If user has Trio in the foreground, we display an in-app banner. If Trio is backgrounded, we push a UserNotification. ## Changes - Adds glucose alarms via user-defined list (urgent-low / low / high / forecasted-low / carbs-required), each with own threshold, schedule, sound, per-window enable, snooze. Hierarchical suppression (urgent-low silences low; low family silences forecasted-low). - Adds `CGMManagerAlertOwnership` gate: when the active CGM provides its own glucose alerts (Dexcom G5 / G6 / One / G7 / One+, plus xDrip4iOS via the `.xdrip` App Group source), reading-driven alarms move into a dedicated "Handled by CGM App" section and the coordinator suppresses them. The "Use CGM App Alerts" toggle is auto-off + disabled when the active CGM has no companion app (e.g. LibreLoop), so users see clearly that Trio owns the alerting. The footer names the responsible app and renders the name as a deep link when a URL scheme is known. - Adds device alarms with three severity tiers (Critical / Time-Sensitive / Normal). Each tier holds multiple configs keyed by Day/Night/Always; pump alerts pick the matching variant. Snooze is per-tier. - Adds `AlertCatalogVendor` protocol + `AlertCatalogRegistry` — a per-pump catalog (Omnipod / Minimed / Dana / Medtrum, incl. Omnipod's dynamic `Fault Event Code 0xNN: …` hex parser) that maps each plugin-emitted `Alert.Identifier` to its `(concept, interruptionLevel, title, category)`. Replaces the previous substring classifier; concept-based dedupe collapses cross-plugin duplicates ("Reservoir Empty" etc.) in the Settings UI. - CGM lifecycle alerts (sensor failure / expiry / signal loss) bypass the catalog and pass through with the plugin's chosen interruption level. - Adds configurable Day & Night Window that is shared across alarms; default day starts 06:00, night starts 22:00 (or the AM/PM equivalent). - Adds sound library of 17 bundled `.caf` tones; per-alarm picker with audible preview, override-Silence-&-Focus toggle. Ported from Loop's `next-dev` branch (thanks @ps2). Alarm row surfaces sound on/off and Overrides-Focus as separate inline tags so "silent but haptic-pierces-Focus" is visible. - Adds critical-audio fallback: `CriticalAlertAudioPlayer` plays via `AVAudioSession(.playback)` + `MPVolumeView` for builds without the Critical Alerts entitlement; iOS otherwise silently downgrades and DnD / silent switch mute the sound. Partially taken from PR #392, inspired by both LoopFollow (thanks @bjorkert) and Loop's `next-dev` (thanks @ps2). - Adds `com.apple.developer.usernotifications.time-sensitive` entitlement so `.timeSensitive` alerts pierce Focus modes. - Replaces the legacy "Not-Looping" monitor with a re-armed delayed alert: every loop success cancels and re-schedules a `delayed(20m)` alert via LoopKit's `Alert.Trigger`. Background-survivable; retracts cleanly when loop and/or app recovers. Skipped automatically when closed loop is off, a manual temp basal is active, or the pump is suspended — those states imply the user isn't expecting auto-enactment. - Adds **Carbs Required** as a configurable `GlucoseAlert` type alongside the existing low/high/forecasted family. Configured under `Settings → Glucose Alarms → Carbs Required` with its own threshold (grams), schedule, sound, snooze, and Override Silence & Focus toggle. The alarm threshold is **independent** from the home-screen tab badge's threshold (which lives in `Settings → Features → UI → Carbs Required Threshold`), so users can have a low-threshold passive badge and a higher-threshold active interrupt. Existing installs get the new alarm backfilled on launch alongside any other types added by later releases. - Add-Alarm picker enforces a one-alarm-per-window constraint per type. Types whose Day & Night coverage is fully occupied (either a single `.always` alarm or both `.day` + `.night` set) show up under an `Unavailable` section in the picker with a footer hint pointing at the existing alarm. The editor's "Active During" dropdown is filtered to options that wouldn't collide. - Adds new in-app banner in iOS-push style; stacked deck with critical-always-on-top, tap or swipe up to snooze 15min by default, long-press for context-menu to snooze (15m / 1h / 3h / 6h). ## Test coverage - Per-pump alert-emission + classification: `Omnipod`, `Minimed`, `Dana`, `Medtrum`, `Tandem`, `RileyLink`. - Catalog: `AlertCatalogRegistryEntriesTests`, `AlertCatalogRegistryOmniFaultTests` (hex-prefix parser). - Glucose alarms: `GlucoseAlertTests`, `GlucoseAlertCoordinatorTests` (incl. carbs-required predicate guards), `GlucoseAlertConfigurationTests` (incl. DST spring-forward / fall-back), `ForecastedGlucoseEvaluatorTests`, `GlucoseAlertsStoreTests` (seed + backfill + Add-picker window gating). - Ownership lookup: `CGMManagerAlertOwnershipTests` (manager + `.xdrip` source paths + deep-link mapping). - Plumbing: `AlertMuterTests`, `DeviceAlertsStoreTests` (variant precedence + per-tier snooze), `TrioAlertCategoryTests`, `TrioModalAlertSchedulerTests`, `NotLoopingMonitorTests`. ## Screenshots | Critical Alert | Time-Sensitive Alert | Info Alert | Snoozing | |--------|--------|--------|--------| | | | | | | Day & Night Windows | Glucose Alarms | Device Alarms | Sound Config (w/ Play) | |--------|--------|--------|--------| | | | | | | Device Alarm Form | Device Alarm Form | Glucose Alarm Form | Glucose Alarm Addition | |--------|--------|--------|--------| | | | | | ## Additional notes - Old per-category settings are gone. Alarms now live in the new modules (`Settings → Glucose Alarms / Device Alarms / Day & Night Window`). - Pump alerts no longer auto-acknowledge; they surface through the unified in-app banner + UserNotification pipeline until the user (or the device) clears them. - Critical interruption level pierces snooze; Time-Sensitive / Active are fully suppressed during a snooze window.

includedPullRequests.title: Move "Snooze All" to Settings and Clean up Legacy Alerting; Follow-Up to #1203 – Prepare O5 and Libre 3/3+ Integration [3/3]
includedPullRequests.body:
NEEDS TO BE MERGED AFTER #1203 LANDS IN `feat/o5` BRANCH.

## Summary

- **Snooze All** moves from a hidden long-press on the home glucose bobble to a prominent button in **Settings → Notifications**. Tapping it opens an inline sheet with the four canonical durations (15 min / 1 hr / 3 hrs / 6 hrs), each calling `TrioAlertManager.applySnooze(for:)` directly.
- **Snooze module deleted.** No more module / router round-trip, no obsolete `GlucoseAlarm` enum, no stray 20 min option.
- **Legacy SwiftMessages alert pipeline removed.** `Router.alertMessage`, `MessageContent`, `MessageType`, `MessageSubtype`, `NotificationAction`, `alertMessageNotificationObserver`, `MainStateModel`'s SwiftMessages dispatch, and the dead `.pumpConfig` UN-tap deep-link are all gone. `SwiftMessages` SwiftPM dependency dropped.
- **4 real callers migrated** to `TrioAlertManager`:
  - Calibration: "Glucose is stale for calibration"
  - GarminManager: "Garmin Connect must be installed"
  - CGM Settings (×2): "Unable to open the app" / "No URL available"
- **`Logger.info()`** is now log-only — matches `warning` / `debug`. Banner side-effect removed.
- **`TimeInterval` convenience helpers** (`init(hours:)`, `init(minutes:)`, getters, statics) extracted from the deleted Snooze module into `Trio/Sources/Helpers/TimeInterval+Convenience.swift`, since callers outside the alert pipeline rely on them.

Net effect: every user-facing alert in the app flows through `TrioAlertManager`. No more parallel SwiftMessages path.

Follow-up to PR #1203.

includedPullRequests.title: Move "Snooze All" to Settings and Clean up Legacy Alerting; Follow-Up to #1203 – Prepare O5 and Libre 3/3+ Integration [3/3]
includedPullRequests.body:
NEEDS TO BE MERGED AFTER #1203 LANDS IN `feat/o5` BRANCH.

## Summary

- **Snooze All** moves from a hidden long-press on the home glucose bobble to a prominent button in **Settings → Notifications**. Tapping it opens an inline sheet with the four canonical durations (15 min / 1 hr / 3 hrs / 6 hrs), each calling `TrioAlertManager.applySnooze(for:)` directly.
- **Snooze module deleted.** No more module / router round-trip, no obsolete `GlucoseAlarm` enum, no stray 20 min option.
- **Legacy SwiftMessages alert pipeline removed.** `Router.alertMessage`, `MessageContent`, `MessageType`, `MessageSubtype`, `NotificationAction`, `alertMessageNotificationObserver`, `MainStateModel`'s SwiftMessages dispatch, and the dead `.pumpConfig` UN-tap deep-link are all gone. `SwiftMessages` SwiftPM dependency dropped.
- **4 real callers migrated** to `TrioAlertManager`:
  - Calibration: "Glucose is stale for calibration"
  - GarminManager: "Garmin Connect must be installed"
  - CGM Settings (×2): "Unable to open the app" / "No URL available"
- **`Logger.info()`** is now log-only — matches `warning` / `debug`. Banner side-effect removed.
- **`TimeInterval` convenience helpers** (`init(hours:)`, `init(minutes:)`, getters, statics) extracted from the deleted Snooze module into `Trio/Sources/Helpers/TimeInterval+Convenience.swift`, since callers outside the alert pipeline rely on them.

Net effect: every user-facing alert in the app flows through `TrioAlertManager`. No more parallel SwiftMessages path.

Follow-up to PR #1203.

includedPullRequests.title: Add a Quick Bolus feature
includedPullRequests.body: Inspired by @bjorkert 's work on Loop Follow, I have added a Quick Bolus feature. **Why?** Users who pre-bolus and/or do not register carbs still have to go through the Treatments sheet, tap the bolus field, add amount, and confirm. When you "just want to bolus", the Treatments sheet is a bit complex. **How does it work?** Tap and hold the + button to open the Quick Bolus feature. It will look at your bolus history for the last 90 days and suggest up to 5 different amounts that you usually give at the same time-of-day. It will distinguish between weekdays and weekends, and give less weight to older bolus data. **Screenshots** If you have no bolus history, it will let you know: Bolus history of 1U and 2U: Quick Bolus suggests 1U and 2U: More historic values: More suggestions: After selecting a value, you are asked to confirm. Biometric control is applied after confirmation. Information/help sheet:

includedPullRequests.title: Use Swift Oref by default
includedPullRequests.body:
This change updates the oref swift setting to be an oref javascript
setting instead, effectively defaulting all users into the Swift
implementation.

By defaulting people into the Swift implementation we will get a
chance to find any lingering issues with the implementation before
removing the Javascript code from the codebase. If there are any
issues, people can switch back to JS without needing to recompile.

includedPullRequests.title: Remove core data fetch limits (already time predicate limited)
includedPullRequests.body:
We had a few fetch limits in place that were potentially leading to fetch results, especially for pump history.

E.g. `getPumpHistory()` uses `pumpHistoryLast24h` but `fetchLimit: 288`.  With TBRs every 5-15 min (96-288/day) plus SMBs and manual user-initiated boluses, there are well over 288 events per day. This could potentially lead to the most‑recent 288 fetch result truncating pump eventing, covering less than 24h.

Similar for fetching glucose, where the predicate did not exclude potential manual glucose entries, leading to a false assumption of one reading per 5 minutes (288(day).

highlights.title: Sensor lifetime indicator on glucose bobble
changes: A colored arc around the glucose bobble drains clockwise to show the sensor's remaining life.
A short tag below the bobble shows time left or a status word like "warming up" or "sensor expired".
Warmup and sensor-failed states hide the arc and show the glucose as a muted "– –".
G7 sensors now count down through the grace period so the bobble's time tag matches the arc.
The glucose simulator adds a Sensor Lifecycle picker so you can preview these sensor states without hardware.

sources.title: nightscout/Trio#1205: Add CGMStatusHighlight Handling: CGM sensor lifetime indicator (arc + tag) – Prepare Libre 3/3+ Integration [2/3]

includedPullRequests.title: Add CGMStatusHighlight Handling: CGM sensor lifetime indicator (arc + tag) – Prepare Libre 3/3+ Integration [2/3]
includedPullRequests.body: ## Summary Adds a sensor lifetime indicator to the home-screen glucose bobble: - **Outer arc** — drains clockwise from 12 o'clock over the sensor's life, sourced from `cgmLifecycleProgress`. Green → orange → red based on `progressState`. - **Tag below the bobble** — short label showing time remaining (`5d 14h`, `22h left`) or a status word (`warming up`, `calibrate`, `sensor expired`, `sensor error`). - Six sensor states: normal / expiring soon / warmup / calibration required / expired / sensor failed. Warmup + failure hide the arc and mute the glucose number to `– –`. - **G7 grace period** — bobble countdown falls back to `sensorEndsAt` once `sensorExpiresAt` passes (was collapsing to `<1m` while the arc still showed ~12h). ‼️ **CAVEAT** This does for users using CGMBLEKit (Dexcom G5/G6/One) through a fork and an addition to CGMBLEKit, not via the current version of the submodule as found in `dev` and `main`. LibreTransmitter has not been tested, should work though. xDrip4iOS will get an update providing us with CGM lifecycle and status highlight _like_ data, but that has not been shipped or checked in to xDrip4iOS yet (thanks to @paulplant for the collab on this) Some Follow-up PRs like needed. --- ## How sensor lifetime is resolved `HomeStateModel.sensorExpiresAt(for:lifecycle:)` resolves the expiration date in this order: 1. **Direct read** when the manager exposes it (e.g., `sensorExpiresAt`). For G7, falls back to `sensorEndsAt` once the primary lifetime has passed so the grace window is counted down instead of clamped to zero. 2. **Reverse-derive** from `activatedAt + percentComplete`: `totalLifetime = elapsed / percentComplete`, `expiresAt = activatedAt + totalLifetime`. includedPullRequests.title: APSManager thread safety fixes (Part 3)
includedPullRequests.body:
Closes the remaining mutable-state race in APSManager around bolus
progress reporting. Final piece split out of the original https://github.com/nightscout/Trio/pull/1145 to have its own architectural discussion.

**BolusProgressState**

  The old `bolusReporter` property was a plain mutable `DoseProgressReporter?`
  mutated from a Combine sink on processQueue (bolusTrigger transitions)
  and concurrently from `cancelBolus` (async context). No isolation.

  Replaced with a private `BolusProgressState` actor that owns the
  reporter and serializes add/remove-observer calls.

**Reorder race in the bolusTrigger sink**

  Pre-change, the sink called `createBolusReporter()` or `clearBolusReporter()`
  directly, both of which were sync. Making them async opens a window
  where two unstructured Tasks (one per emission) could reorder against
  each other at the actor — unstructured Tasks enter an actor in
  scheduler order, not the order they were spawned. A fast bolus
  end-then-start transition (real in practice) could land setReporter
  before its matching clear and wipe the fresh reporter.

  Both transitions are now funneled through a single Task per sink
  emission, awaiting in-order at the actor.

**doseProgressReporterDidUpdate**

  The `DoseProgressObserver` protocol method is sync, so the call to
  `clearBolusReporter()` (now async) is wrapped in a Task. The race that
  would normally make this dangerous is exactly what the generation
  token in BolusProgressState protects against.

includedPullRequests.title: Refresh stale persistent history token for CoreData
includedPullRequests.body:
When Trio calls `fetchPersistentHistory` it logs errors. One type of
error, the `NSPersistentHistoryTokenExpiredError` error will cause
Trio to stop refreshing data. This error can happen for a few reasons,
like not using Trio of a while or updating the database.

The fix is to refresh all objects manually and reset the persistent
history token, i.e., `lastHistoryToken` stored in UserDefaults.

This error is extremely hard to test, but I had a device stuck in this
state and confirmed the fix.

includedPullRequests.title: Make sure that autosens has a profile to work with
includedPullRequests.body:
The Swift version of autosens expects to have a profile object, so if
you start with oref-swift from the start the current version will
throw an exception on autosens since there is no profile, and the
algorithm will never make progress.

This change swaps the order of autosens and profile creation. Profile
creation doesn't depend on autosens, so this change is safe and
enables systems set up as oref-swift from the start run.

Note: There was a tiny amount of parallelism in the previous version,
but not enough to justify so I removed it to make the code more
straightforward.

Thanks to @mountrcg for reporting this originally.

highlights.title: Prevent duplicate loops and tidy background tasks
changes: Trio will no longer start two loop cycles at the same time.

sources.title: APSManager thread safety fixes Part 2: LoopGuard actor + background-task lifecycle

includedPullRequests.title: APSManager thread safety fixes (Part 2)
includedPullRequests.body:
Closes the loop-serialization race and reworks the background-task
lifecycle around the loop's async scope. Sequel to Part 1, split out
of the original https://github.com/nightscout/Trio/pull/1145 to discuss LoopGuard + background-task handling separately from the bolus-progress actor.

**LoopGuard**

  The old check-then-act pattern read `isLooping.value`, returned from
  `canStartNewLoop()`, then later (after a suspension point) called
  `isLooping.send(true)`. Two concurrent `recommendsLoop` events could
  both observe `false` before either had sent `true`, so loop() could
  run twice. Replaced by a private `LoopGuard` actor that performs the
  check-and-mark-running step as a single atomic operation. isLooping
  becomes a downstream notification mechanism.

**Background-task lifecycle**

Removed the Task in the expiration handler which didn't provide a guarantee to be executed. Aligned with the example in https://developer.apple.com/documentation/uikit/extending-your-app-s-background-execution-time. Side note: we probably need to refactor this when moving to Swift 6 as the expiration handler closure is Sendable and captures and mutates the var backgroundTaskID which isn't allowed when strict concurrency checking is on.

**Loop lifecycle consolidation**

  `canStartNewLoop`, `setupLoop`, `loopCompleted` are folded into
  loop() and a new single-exit-point `finalizeLoop`. `executeLoop` no
  longer calls finalize itself; the caller owns lifecycle. Open and
  closed loop paths in executeLoop now share the stats-recording
  block, with `enactDetermination` gated by `settings.closedLoop` at
  the end.

  `calculateLoopInterval` now takes `loopStartDate` as a parameter
  instead of reading the instance `lastLoopStartDate` — keeps the
  helper independent of the surrounding mutation order in loop().

This will be the first of at least 3 Pull requests targeted at optimizing the thread safety of the APSManager. As suggested by @kingst in PR #1145 I splitted my initial PR in several smaller PRs to be able to better review the changes made.

Changes made in this PR:

- remove unused `viewContext`
- move `tir()` out of a nested perform closure
- add `[weak self]` to combine sinks and `privateContext` perform closures
- move combine operations to receive on the main thread to avoid race conditions

includedPullRequests.title: Remove unused convertGlucose function
includedPullRequests.body:
This PR removes an unused function from the core determine basal logic in oref-swift: `convertGlucose`. In the original JS implementation, several output properties and reason string values are run through a `convert_bg` function that converts the glucose value to `mmol` based on the `profile.outUnits` value.

However, `profile.outUnits` is always in `.mgdl`, and should always be in `.mgdl` so we should remove this function. The path goes:
- The convert function branches based on the value of `profile.outUnits`
- `profile.outUnits` is set from `bgTarget.userPreferredUnits`
- all of the write paths for the file that saves the `bgTarget` value store these values as mg/dl and hard code `userPreferredUnits` to `.mgdl`.

Unit tests still pass with this change.

includedPullRequests.title: Port oref0 Algorithm from Javascript to Swift
includedPullRequests.body:
## Summary

Native Swift port of Trio's [JS-based oref0 algorithm](https://github.com/nightscout/trio-oref), replacing the JavaScript bridge with a first-class Swift implementation across all core algorithm modules: IOB, Meal, Autosens, and DetermineBasal (including Dynamic ISF).

### Background
Trio has historically executed its dosing algorithm by calling into a bundled JavaScript runtime (`trio-oref`). This port replaces that execution path end-to-end in Swift, removing the JS bridge dependency for users who — currently! — opt in. The port was developed between February 2025 and April 2026.

More details to be added at later point. The research paper produced in connection with this port will be provided at a later date.

###  Verification
Parity between the JavaScript and Swift implementations was verified through:

* **Mechanistic in silico simulation**: structural comparison of algorithm logic
* **Shadow execution replay**: 736,480 real-world algorithm invocations were replayed through both implementations and their outputs compared, covering all Swift modules

Notable behaviours verified include: IoB with long pump suspends, zombie carb detection, `currentDeviation` null handling in meal, `avgDelta` and `getGlucoseStatus` rounding, Dynamic ISF `tddRatio` / `insulinFactor` / `sensitivityRatio` outputs, and `expectedDelta` edge cases.

### Enabling

This is **opt-in**. The JavaScript path remains the default and is unchanged.

**Settings → Algorithm → Additionals → Use Swift Oref**

- **Off** (default): algorithm runs entirely in JavaScript, JS outputs drive insulin dosing
- **On**: algorithm runs entirely in Swift, Swift outputs drive insulin dosing

When enabled, a green `Swift Oref` badge appears in the Loop Status view to make it clear which path is active.

### Publication relating to this port 
Screven, T., Zhu, Z., Cengiz, D., Lal, R. A., Hood, K. K., & King, S. T. (2026). [*A Principled Framework for Safe Algorithm Updates in Automated Insulin Delivery Systems*](https://arxiv.org/html/2606.13882v1). arXiv:2606.13882v1.

includedPullRequests.title: Fix: Floor CGM glucose at 39 mg/dL in GlucoseStorage
includedPullRequests.body:
## Summary

Addresses nightscout/Trio-dev#631 — since LibreTransmitter ignores Abbott given limits and propagates raw glucose, oref can receive values below the official 39 mg/dL CGM floor (LibreTransmitter explicitly bypasses the Libre algorithm's floor, forwarding values down to 1 mg/dL). On dev those sub-39 readings are silently dropped by the JS oref glucose-get-last filter (>38), leaving determination with no fresh BG and the pump stuck in whatever temp it was last on. The reporter saw ~1h 7min of no Swift determinations with a BG nadir of 23 mg/dL.

This PR adds a defensive chokepoint in BaseGlucoseStorage:

  - New Config.minimumGlucose = 39 and a private clampToMinimum(_:) helper that clamps both glucose and sgv on each
  BloodGlucose, emitting debug(.deviceManager, ...) with the raw value and timestamp so the original reading is preserved
  in support logs.
  - storeGlucose and backfillGlucose both run their input through clampToMinimum before any filtering or persistence.
  storeCGMState receives the clamped array too.
  - addManualGlucose is intentionally left untouched — user-entered fingerstick values are not silently rewritten.

  The floor aligns with BloodGlucose.isStateValid (already sgv >= 39) and FetchGlucoseManager.minimumSmoothedGlucose: 39.

includedPullRequests.title: Change fetchLimit for glucose oref input to be dynamic based on maxMealAbsorptionTime #920
includedPullRequests.body:
## Summary
The glucose history fed into the meal/COB algorithm was capped at a fixed fetchLimit: 72 (72 readings × 5 min = 6h).
That constant predates the user-selectable maxMealAbsorptionTime (MMAT) setting, which ranges 4–10h. When MMAT exceeds 6h, the COB calculation considers carb absorption out to MMAT hours but only has 6h of glucose to work with.

The result is the bug reported in #920: mealCOB rises after a carb entry (to an amount larger than the carbs entered)
as larger absorption buckets slide out the back of the 6h window and are replaced by smaller front buckets, then crashes to zero when the meal is evicted at mealTime + MMAT. This drives over-bolusing and hypo risk.

This affects both the JS oref0 path and the native oref-swift port, since the limit is applied upstream in OpenAPS.determineBasal before either path runs.

The fix makes the fetch limit dynamic: ceil(maxMealAbsorptionTime × 12) readings, so the glucose window always covers the full absorption window. Preferences are loaded up front (the existing async load is just hoisted and reused) to derive the limit before the parallel fetches. Tying it to the setting rather than a static cap means it can't silently drift again if the MMAT range changes.

Credit to @robertjwellwood for the diagnosis and simulation in #920.

## To Test

  - Build and run with default MMAT (6h), then verify COB behaves as before
  - Set MMAT to 8–10h, enter a carb dose, and confirm COB decays smoothly toward 0 without rising above the entered amount or cliff-dropping
  - Verify both useSwiftOref on and off produce consistent COB trajectories (so JS-based oref and native Swift port)
  - Confirm glucoseFetchLimit scales as expected (4h→48, 6h→72, 10h→120)
